'''Joan Josep Guinovart Cirera''' (3 July 1947 – 1 January 2025) was a Spanish biochemist known for  research on glycogen and liver glycogen synthase, as well as for work in [[FEBS]], [[IUBMB]] and the Spanish Society of Biochemistry and Molecular Biology.

== Personal life ==
Joan Guinovart was born on 3 July 1947 in [[Tarragona]], Spain<ref name = sac>Societat Andorrana de Ciàncies, May–June 2008, "Joan Josep Guinovart
i Cirera" (in Catalan), https://web.archive.org/web/20141220223710/http://www.sac.ad/el%20sac%20pdf/elsac137.pdf</ref> and died on 1 January 2025 in [[Barcelona]].<ref name = vang>La Vanguardia, "Muere el científico Joan Guinovart, fundador del IRB Barcelona", https://www.lavanguardia.com/vida/20250101/10250408/muere-cientifico-joan-guinovart-fundador-irb-barcelona.html</ref> He was married to Rosa-Francisca Florensa.<ref>{{cite web 
| url = https://www.elvallenc.cat/noticia/348/el-dr-joan-j-guinovart-pronuncia-una-conferencia-a-la-cambra
| publisher = El Vallenc
| title = El Dr. Joan J. Guinovart pronuncia una conferència a la Cambra
|year = 2009
}}</ref> They lived in Barcelona, with frequent visits to a house designed and built for them in 2010 in [[Canejan]], [[Val d'Aran]],<ref>{{cite web 
| url = https://www.archdaily.com/65555/guinovart-florensa-residence-cadaval-sola-morales
| title = Guinovart Florensa Residence / Cadaval & Solà-Morales
| publisher = archdaly | year = 2010
}}</ref> close to the border with France. Their daughter Caterina is a biomedical researcher  on malaria at the [[Barcelona Biomedical Research Park#Overview|ISGlobal institute]].<ref name = obit>{{cite web | url = https://www.lavanguardia.com/ciencia/20250102/10252115/ciencia-le-debe-joan-guinovart-fallecido-1-enero.html
| publisher = La Vanguardia
|title = Obituario: Lo que la ciencia le debe a Joan Guinovart, fallecido a los 77 años
| year = 2025
| access-date =  8 January 2025| author = Josep Corbella
}}</ref>

== Education ==
Guinovart qualified in pharmacy and chemical sciences at the [[University of Barcelona]] in 1969, and was awarded a doctorate in pharmacy by the same university in 1973.<ref name =sac /> He then spent the years 1974–1975 as a post-doctoral fellow in the department of pharmacology of the [[University of Virginia]].<ref name =sac /> There he encountered a scientific environment in which young researchers were encouraged to think for themselves, in contrast to the culture of obedience that he had known before.<ref name = obit/>

== Career ==
Guinovart started his career as assistant professor of clinical biochemistry at the Prínceps d'Espanya Hospital in [[Bellvitge]] (1978–1980). He became chief of the clinical analysis service of the Social Security  (1980–1985). He was assistant professor (later full professor) of biochemistry at the Faculty of Pharmacy of the University of Barcelona (1975–1983) and at the Faculty of Veterinary Medicine of the [[Autonomous University of Barcelona]] (1983–1985).<ref name = sac/>

He held the chairs of biochemistry and molecular biology at the Autonomous University of Barcelona from 1986 to 1990, and the University of Barcelona from 1990, and was the director of the Department of Biochemistry and Molecular Biology at the University of Barcelona from 1995 to 2001.<ref name = sac/>

During his teaching career Guinovart supervised many doctoral students, beginning with [[Joan Massagué]],<ref name = massag/> Fàtima Bosch<ref name = ciudad/> and Carlos Ciudad.<ref name = ciudad/>

From 1992 to 1993 he was visiting professor at the Department of Biochemistry and Biophysics at the  [[University of California, San Francisco]].<ref name = sac/>

In 2001–2002 he was director general of the [[Barcelona Science Park]], where he created the [[Institute for Research in Biomedicine]] (IRB Barcelona) in 2005, which he directed until 2018.<ref name = sac/>

== Service to international unions and scientific societies ==
Guinovart was president of the Spanish Society of Biochemistry and Molecular Biology (SEBBM) from 1996 to 2000, and in this capacity he presided over  the organizing committee of the FEBS Congress in Barcelona in 1996. He was a member of executive committee of FEBS from 1997 to 2005.<ref name=sac/> He was president of the IUBMB from 2015 to 2018, and president of the Confederation of Scientific Societies of Spain (COSCE) from 2005 to 2011.<ref name=sac/>

He was the founding editor-in-chief of the magazine ''SEBBM'',<ref name = diplome/> and editor of ''IUBMB Life'', and was a regular contributor to ''[[La Vanguardia]]'', the leading newspaper of [[Catalonia]].<ref name=sac/>

== Honours ==
Guinovart received many honours and awards during his career, starting with the Leandre Cervera Prize of the Catalan Society of Biology (1979 and 1985), <!--followed by the medal of the French Society of Biochemistry and Molecular Biology (1983),--> and the Narcís Monturiol Prize of the [[Generalitat of Catalonia]] (1999).<ref name = sac/> He received the medal of the Spanish Society of Biochemistry and Molecular Biology as an Honorary Member.<ref>{{cite web 
| url = https://sebbm.es/equipo/socios-de-honor/page/8/
| publisher = Spanish Society of Biochemistry and Molecular Biology (SEBBM)
|title = Socios de Honor
}}</ref> In 2021 he received the IUBMB Distinguished Service Award.<ref>{{cite web 
| url = https://iubmb.org/congratulations-to-prof-joan-guinovart/
| publisher = International Union of Biochemistry and Molecular Biology (IUBMB)
|title = Congratulations to Professor Joan Guinovart
| date = 25 July 2021
}}</ref> After a lifetime of "contribution to the molecular biosciences community" FEBS in 2024 awarded him the first Israel Pecht Award.<ref>{{cite web 
| title = The Israel Pecht Award 2024
| date = 26 April 2024
| publisher = Federation of European Biochemical Societies (FEBS)
| url = https://www.febs.org/news/the-israel-pecht-award-2024-febs-recognition-award-for-outstanding-contribution-to-the-molecular-biosciences-community/
}}</ref> He had previously received the Diplôme d'Honneur
of FEBS in 2007.<ref name = diplome>{{cite web 
| url = https://www.febs.org/news/in-memory-of-professor-joan-j-guinovart-his-legacy-and-significant-contributions-to-febs/
| publisher = Federation of European Biochemical Societies (FEBS)
| title = in memory of Professor Joan J. Guinovart: his legacy and significant contributions to FEBS
| date = 2 January 2025
}}</ref>

In 2005 he was elected as a Corresponding Member of the Chilean Academy of Sciences (the photograph at the beginning of this article was taken at the time of his admission),<ref>{{cite web 
| url = https://www.academiadeciencias.cl/miembros-correspondientes-extranjeros/
| title = Miembros Correspondientes extranjeros
| publisher = Academia Chilena de Ciencias
}}</ref> in 2006 to the Royal Academy of Pharmacy of Spain,<ref>{{cite web 
| url = https://ranf.com/academicos-de-numero-actual/page/2/
| publisher = Real Academia Nacional de Farmacia
| title = Académicos de Número Actual
}}</ref> and in 2011 to the Academia Europaea.<ref>{{cite web 
| url = https://ae-info.org/ae/Acad_Main/List_of_Members?
| publisher = Academia Europaea: the Academy of Europe
| title = List of Members
}}</ref>
